pages.text: "When will the snow stop?" Nils the little bear pressed his nose to the window and looked out. Snow fell so thickly that even the trees were hard to see. The forest was all white.
"I want to go outside and jump in the snow..." Nils rested his chin on the windowsill. The snow showed no sign of stopping.
Nils paced by the window, stamping his feet. "I am bored—has it still not stopped?" Grandpa Bruno added another log to the stove.
Nils pulled the covers over himself, then pulled them off again. Outside the window, everything was still white. "I cannot do anything today." He flopped onto the floor.
Grandpa brought a lamp and set it in front of the wall. Then he held his broad palm upright in front of the lamp. A huge dark shape appeared on the wall.
"Wow, a bear!" Nils jumped up. Grandpa moved his palm, and the bear on the wall opened its mouth wide. "Bored? Play with shadows!" Grandpa laughed heartily.
Nils held his little curled paw in front of the lamp too. A round rabbit appeared on the wall with its ears sticking up. "Bored? Play with shadows! My rabbit is faster!" Nils giggled.
The rabbit hopped, the bear lumbered, and they played tag on the wall. The smallest movement of Nils's paw made the rabbit leap. With just one lamp, the whole wall became a story.
"One, hold your paw in front of the lamp! Two, watch the wall! Three, move and make a story!" Nils made rabbits and birds by himself. Before he knew it, not a snowflake remained outside.

Grandpa patted Nils's back and opened the door wide. Nils raised both paws above his head. Boring time passes quickly when you turn it into play. "Let us play again after I run outside! Bored? Play with shadows!"
